fact: Xalam Analytics says the Projet de Couverture Nationale fibre project is underway, about 3,000 km of terrestrial fibre connecting key towns; document gives no event date, so its published date (January 2026) is used.

The Treasury sheet says the PCN deployed about 3,000 km of fibre linking Pointe-Noire, Dolisie, Brazzaville, Oyo and Ouesso, operated and marketed by Congo Telecom, plus a 1,100 km secondary E2C network.
Ecofin reports Congo launched construction of a second national fibre backbone in September 2023, to link Pointe-Noire and Brazzaville, with no recent progress update.
Xalam Analytics says the Projet de Couverture Nationale fibre project is underway, about 3,000km of terrestrial fibre connecting key towns, alongside the ongoing Central African Backbone project.

AfriqueITNews reports the Congolese government entrusted Silicone Connect under a public-private partnership with upgrading the national fibre network between Pointe-Noire and Brazzaville to 200 Gb, a EUR 3.2 million project launched on 12 July 2024.
AfriqueITNews reports the first phase, the southern backbone, was completed, moving from SDH to DWDM on the existing Pointe-Noire to Brazzaville fibre network.
